name: Seismic design of process facilities
principle: In seismic regions, structures, equipment, piping and their connections are designed for earthquake demands: site-specific hazard analysis, response spectrum or time-history analysis, anchorage and support design for equipment, and settlement or fault-movement checks for tanks and pipelines. Codes (ASCE 7, EN 1998, and industry guides such as ASCE 4 and API 650 Appendix E) tier the objectives — keep safety systems functional, prevent release of hazardous inventory, allow economic damage elsewhere. Performance-based methods and base isolation are used where downtime cost dominates.

process_steps.name: Seismic hazard characterised for the site
Structures and equipment analysed for code or project spectra
Anchorage, supports and connections detailed for the demand
Qualification by analysis, test or experience documented

limitations: equipment qualification for safety systems can dominate cost in high-hazard regions
liquefaction and slope-failure checks frequently govern over the structural analysis itself
advantages: keeps hazardous inventory contained and safety systems running through the design event
performance-based design can cut cost by matching design effort to consequence
